questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Cat  |  Dog  |  Lion  |  Tiger  |  Rose
questions.explanation: D is correct. Cat, Dog, Lion, and Tiger are all animals (mammals). Rose is a flowering plant. The odd one out is Rose. Classification: Four belong to Kingdom Animalia; Rose belongs to Kingdom Plantae.

questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Venus  |  Mars  |  Sun  |  Jupiter  |  Saturn
questions.explanation: C is correct. Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn are planets in our solar system. The Sun is a star — the central body around which planets orbit. Trap: students may think of all of them as celestial bodies, but the classification planet vs. star is the key distinction.

questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Kilometer  |  Meter  |  Kilogram  |  Centimeter  |  Millimeter
questions.explanation: C is correct. Kilometer, Meter, Centimeter, and Millimeter are all units of length/distance. Kilogram is a unit of mass. The odd one out is Kilogram. Trap: the 'kilo-' prefix in Kilogram and Kilometer might mislead students into thinking they belong to the same category — but units must be compared by what they measure, not their prefix.

questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Cricket  |  Football  |  Hockey  |  Chess  |  Basketball
questions.explanation: D is correct. Cricket, Football, Hockey, and Basketball are all team sports played outdoors requiring physical activity. Chess is an indoor board game requiring no physical movement. The odd one out is Chess. Trap: all of the options are sports/games — the distinction is physical team sport vs. indoor strategy game.

questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Copper  |  Gold  |  Iron  |  Steel  |  Silver
questions.explanation: D is correct. Copper, Gold, Iron, and Silver are all pure metals (chemical elements). Steel is an alloy — a mixture of iron and carbon (along with other elements). The odd one out is Steel. Trap: all five look like metals and are used in similar contexts, but the pure element vs. alloy distinction is key.

questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Pen  |  Pencil  |  Chalk  |  Marker  |  Eraser
questions.explanation: D is correct. Pen, Pencil, Chalk, and Marker are all writing instruments used to make marks. An Eraser is used to remove written marks, not to create them — it is a correction tool. The odd one out is Eraser. Trap: all items relate to writing/classroom use, but function determines the category.

questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Violin  |  Guitar  |  Sitar  |  Flute  |  Harp
questions.explanation: D is correct. Violin, Guitar, Sitar, and Harp are all chordophone (string) instruments — they produce sound by vibrating strings. Flute is an aerophone (wind instrument) — it produces sound by blowing air across an opening. The odd one out is Flute. Trap: students often group all traditional instruments together without distinguishing string vs. wind categories.

questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Osmosis  |  Diffusion  |  Transpiration  |  Mitosis  |  Active Transport
questions.explanation: D is correct. Osmosis, Diffusion, Transpiration, and Active Transport are all processes involving the movement of substances (water, molecules, ions) across membranes or through organisms. Mitosis is a process of cell division — it is about cell reproduction, not substance transport. The odd one out is Mitosis. Trap: all are biological processes, but transport vs. cell division is the critical distinction.

questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Mercury  |  Venus  |  Comet  |  Neptune  |  Saturn
questions.explanation: C is correct. Mercury, Venus, Neptune, and Saturn are all planets that orbit the Sun in stable, nearly circular paths. A Comet is a small icy body with a highly elliptical orbit around the Sun — not a planet. The odd one out is Comet. Trap: all are members of our solar system, but planets and comets differ fundamentally in size, composition, orbit shape, and origin.

questions.stem:
Find the odd one out:
Oak  |  Teak  |  Bamboo  |  Walnut  |  Mango
questions.explanation: C is correct. Oak, Teak, Walnut, and Mango are all dicotyledonous trees (woody plants with broad leaves). Bamboo belongs to the Poaceae family (grasses) — it is botanically a grass, not a tree, despite its tree-like appearance and woody stems. The odd one out is Bamboo. Trap: Bamboo looks like a tree and is used as wood, but it is scientifically classified as a grass (monocotyledon).
